title: decree machine
description: A decree machine: a YAML statechart in .decree/machines/<name>.yml, one W3C SCXML document written as YAML. It holds only structure: states, what each state invokes, and transitions from events to states; never code or paths. Every state invokes one function (a script, a check, a model, a person or another machine), and the function's result is an event that picks the next state. This schema checks the shape: keys, types, required keys, each invoke kind and condition, name patterns and ranges. `decree check` checks the rest (V1-V21): that names resolve, targets exist, every state is reachable, and no machine invokes itself. Reference: docs/reference/machines.md.

name.description: SCXML <scxml name>. The machine's name: must equal the file stem (`hello` in machines/hello.yml) and match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ (V1).

description.description: What the machine does, in one sentence. Required. Used in prompts, `decree status` and graphs.
examples: Implement one feature spec with an AI agent, verify it, and commit.

data.description: SCXML <datamodel>: the machine's typed, read-only values, by name. A message's `params` override the defaults for one run; nothing else changes them. Conditions read them as `{ data: <name> }`, and scripts as DECREE_DATA_<NAME>.

onentry.description: Extension (SCXML's <scxml> has none): scripts run once when the run starts, in order, and again when `decree process --retry` continues it. They produce no event; a failure raises `error`.

onexit.description: Extension (SCXML's <scxml> has none): scripts run once, in order, after a root-level final state is entered. They produce no event.

initial.description: SCXML <scxml initial>: the state the run starts in. Must be a direct child in `states` (V3).

states.description: SCXML child <state> and <final> elements: the root-level states, by id. Every machine has a root-level final state named `failed` (V5): an unhandled `error` goes there. State ids match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and are unique across the whole machine (V2).

failed.description: The root-level final state an unhandled `error` goes to. Every machine has it (V5).

duration.description: A whole number of at most 9 digits followed by one unit: s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours) or d (days). No fractions, no combinations such as 1h30m, and no bare numbers (docs/reference/machines.md, Durations).

stateId.description: A state id: a bare id, never a path. State ids are unique across the whole machine (V2).

machineName.description: A machine's name: the stem of its file in .decree/machines/.

scriptName.description: A script name, never a path. It resolves to exactly one executable file: scripts/<machine>/<name> or scripts/<name>, with or without one extension such as .sh (V12).

question.description: What is being decided, written to stand alone: the model or the person sees exactly this question and the options with their descriptions (V8). Write it in block style, one key per line.

dataSpec.description: One `data` entry, SCXML <data id>: its type and its default, which must match the type (V14).

default.description: The value when a message's `params` does not set it. Required, and of the entry's `type` (V14).

states.description: A compound state's child states, by id. Ids match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and are unique across the whole machine (V2).

state.description: An SCXML state, of one of three kinds. Atomic: does one step, its `invoke`, and its result is an event that picks a transition. Compound: has child `states` and an `initial`, and no `invoke`. Final (`final: true`): ends its parent; a root-level final state ends the run. Keys go in this order: description, invoke, onentry, onexit, transitions, emits, then initial and states.

final.description: SCXML <final>: `final: true` marks a final state. Final states may only have `description`, `onentry` and `emits` (V7). Entering a root-level final state ends the run; a nested one raises done.state.<parent id>.

description.description: Extension: what the state is for. Shown as a `person` state's question when it waits, and in graphs.

onentry.description: SCXML <onentry>: scripts run, in order, every time this state is entered. They produce no event; a failure raises `error` after entry completes.

onexit.description: SCXML <onexit>: scripts run, in order, every time this state is exited. Not allowed on final states (V7).

emits.description: Extension: the machines this state's scripts may queue messages for with `decree emit` (V13). Enforced by `decree emit`, drawn by `decree graph`.

initial.description: SCXML <state initial>: on a compound state, the child entered first. Must be a direct child in `states` (V3). Present together with `states`, absent on every other state (V6).

finalState.description: A final state may only have `final`, `description`, `onentry` and `emits` (V7).

compoundState.description: A compound state has `initial` and `states`, and no `invoke` (V6).

atomicState.description: An atomic state: no `initial` without `states` (V6), and no `type: internal` transition, which only a compound state may have (V17). A `check` state's events are `true` and `false`, never `yes` and `no` (V8). A `model` or `person` state needs at least two options, each with a `description` (V8), none of them a reserved event (V18).

invoke.description: SCXML <invoke>: the state's function. Its result is one event that picks the next transition. Either a script name (`invoke: build` is short for `invoke: { script: build }`), or a map with exactly one key naming the kind: `script`, `check`, `model`, `person` or `machine`. A state with no invoke and a `done` transition passes straight through. Not allowed on compound (V6) or final (V7) states.

anyOf.title: script name
anyOf.description: Short for `{ script: <name> }`: run this script. Exit 0 is `done`, non-zero is `error`, or the event the script writes to $DECREE_EVENT_FILE (`echo pass > "$DECREE_EVENT_FILE"`).

model.question: Should we implement again or split the work?

scriptInvoke.description: SCXML type decree:script. Run a script (docs/reference/scripts.md). Events: `done` (exit 0), `error` (non-zero), or the event the script writes to `$DECREE_EVENT_FILE`. A bare name is short for `{ name: <name> }`.

max_attempts.description: How many times to run a script that fails, in place: same state, no onexit or onentry between attempts. Default 1 (no retry). A transition back to an earlier state is a different thing: a new round the machine chooses.

timeout.description: How long each attempt may run before decree stops it; a timed-out attempt fails. A duration (V16). Default: no limit.

modelInvoke.description: SCXML type decree:model. A router machine asks a model to pick one of this state's transitions (its options: every transition except `unsure` and `error`, each with a `description`). Events: the chosen option; `unsure` if its confidence is below `min_confidence`; `error` if the router fails or replies with something that is not an option.

router.description: The router machine that asks the model. Default: the machine named `router`, which `decree init` writes (V16).

min_confidence.description: From 0 to 1 (V16). Below it the decision is `unsure`, which the state must then handle, itself or through an ancestor (V8).

output.description: A state with a script invoke (V9) whose latest output, as logged, the model is shown. Without it the model sees only the message body.

examples.question: Should we implement again or split the work?

personInvoke.description: SCXML type decree:person. The `ask` script tells someone; the run pauses until a reply (`decree event <wait id> <option>`) picks one of this state's transitions (its options: every transition except `unsure` and `error`, each with a `description`). Events: the chosen option; `error` on timeout.

ask.description: The script that tells someone a decision is waiting and how to reply. It gets the wait id and the options in its environment (V12).

timeout.description: How long to wait for a reply; after that the event is `error`. A duration (V16). Default: wait forever.

machineInvoke.description: SCXML's own invoke type: run another machine as a child run. Its event is the id of the root-level final state the child reached (`done`, `rejected`, ...), and `failed` becomes `error`; this state must handle each of them (V8). A bare name is short for `{ name: <name> }`. A machine never invokes itself, directly or through others (V20).

params.description: Sets the child's `data` for this run, like SCXML <invoke><param>. Each name must be a `data` entry of the child, with a value of its type (V16).

condition.description: SCXML type decree:check: decree evaluates a condition, with no AI. Events: `true` or `false`. A condition has exactly one subject (`output`, `data`, `visits` or `confidence`) and exactly one operator that subject takes (V10). There is no and/or: to test two things, use two check states in a row.

output.description: Subject: the latest script output, as logged, of this state, which must have a script invoke (V9). Takes `matches` only.

data.description: Subject: this `data` value. Takes the comparison operators, with a value of its type, and `matches` when its type is `string` (V10).

visits.description: Subject: how many times this atomic state was entered in this run. Takes the comparison operators, with an int or `{ data: <name> }`.

confidence.description: Subject: the latest `model` decision's confidence in this `model` state, 0 to 1 (0 if the router reported none). Takes the comparison operators, with a number from 0 to 1.

matches.description: Operator: the subject (`output`, or `string` data) matches this regular expression, in the Rust regex crate's syntax; it matches anywhere unless anchored ((?i) for case-insensitive). Quote it in YAML.

equals.description: Operator: the subject equals this value: a literal or `{ data: <name> }`.

not_equals.description: Operator: the subject does not equal this value: a literal or `{ data: <name> }`.

less_than.description: Operator: the subject is less than this value: an int (a number from 0 to 1 for `confidence`) or `{ data: <name> }`.

at_most.description: Operator: the subject is at most this value: an int (a number from 0 to 1 for `confidence`) or `{ data: <name> }`.

more_than.description: Operator: the subject is more than this value: an int (a number from 0 to 1 for `confidence`) or `{ data: <name> }`.

at_least.description: Operator: the subject is at least this value: an int (a number from 0 to 1 for `confidence`) or `{ data: <name> }`.

value.description: A literal (an int, a string or a bool) or `{ data: <name> }`, of the same type as the subject's data (V10). Ordering operators compare ints only.

intValue.description: An int, or `{ data: <name> }` naming int data.

transitions.description: SCXML <transition event target>: event name to target state. For an event, decree checks the current state's transitions, then each ancestor's, innermost first; a transition matches its event or one that extends it after a `.` (`done.state` matches `done.state.work`). An unhandled `error` goes to the root-level `failed`; any other unhandled event becomes `error`. Event names match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$ (V18); `true:` and `false:` unquoted are the events `true` and `false`. Not allowed on final states (V7).

transition.description: A target state id (short form, `event: target`), or the long form `{ target, description?, type? }`.

target.description: The state this event leads to: a bare state id anywhere in the machine (V4).

description.description: What choosing this option means. Required on each option of a `model` or `person` state (V8): the model or person sees it. Write it in block style.

type.description: SCXML `type: internal`: a compound state's transition to one of its descendants that neither exits nor re-enters the compound state (V17). Omitted means external.

examples.description: The failures look fixable; implement again.

options.description: A `model` or `person` state's transitions. Its options are every transition except `unsure` and `error`: at least two, each with a `description`, none named `done` or starting with `done.` or `error.` (V8, V18).

option.description: An option of a `model` or `person` state, in the long form with a `description` (V8).
